key_insight: Distributed QAOA sampling, combined with classical repair and partitioning, can scale quantum-assisted optimization to thousand-variable constrained problems on current quantum hardware.
engineering_relevance: The workflow offers a practical route for large-scale scheduling and energy-trading optimization by making quantum sampling executable through graph partitioning and circuit packing.
method: Spectrally partition the matching problem into hardware-sized subproblems.
Run single-layer QAOA sampling on each partition, then apply greedy feasibility repair.
Use E-FCFW to assemble sparse weighted matchings into the final Minimum Birkhoff Decomposition.
evidence_signal: On the PEGASE-1354 benchmark, repaired QAOA samples outperformed simulated annealing and random sampling, with the best hardware run using a 50-qubit partition and spatial packing cutting execution time by about 3×.
watch_item: Smaller partitions such as 20 qubits reduce convergence quality, and heavy MPS truncation can degrade candidate quality, so preserving enough quantum structure per partition remains important.
paper_title: Scaling Quantum Optimization to the Thousand-Qubit Scale with Distributed Quantum Sampling
